sections.h2: How fast has Clermont grown, and how does that touch a sale?
sections.html:
Lake County's Clermont counted 28,742 people in 2010, 43,021 in 2020 and 52,812 in the July 2025 estimate, so the city grew 22.8% above its 2020 base in just over five years. Children under 18 are 22.0% of residents, which fits a town of families who moved in for jobs and schools elsewhere in the region.

Newer neighborhoods change the seller's checklist. Roof, plumbing and permit records tend to be fresh on a recent build, while a house with unpermitted work needs sorting out before closing.

sections.h2: What do federal housing numbers show for Clermont?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied Clermont home was valued at $418,400 for 2020 through 2024, and owners live in 68.1% of the housing.

  • Households: 17,609, averaging 2.64 people.
  • Monthly owner costs: $2,120 with a mortgage, $655 without.
  • Gross rent, median: $1,828 a month.
  • Household income, median: $82,306.
  • Travel time to work: 31.3 minutes.

A commute that long gives buyers a reason to ask about roads and drive times at a showing.

sections.h2: Is my Clermont mailing address inside the city limits?
sections.html:
Not always. The city tells owners that a Clermont mailing address does not prove a parcel lies within city limits, and it points them to the Lake County Property Appraiser site: search the address, open the Alternate Key, and read the millage group. A plain number marks unincorporated Lake County, while letters such as GR or MI mark Groveland or Minneola.

The answer decides which building department issued your permits, which codes applied and which tax bill you will split at closing. Confirm it first, then gather permits from the right office.

sections.h2: What permit questions arise when a Clermont house goes on the market?
sections.html:
The city's Building Services FAQ says almost everything may need a permit, with exceptions such as replacing kitchen cabinets, flooring and painting. Homeowners can pull their own permit only if they own and occupy the residence, and they sign an owner-builder affidavit. The city also warns that a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself may be a red flag.

Buyers and their inspectors compare visible work to the record. Items the FAQ names:

  • Fences need a permit, including repair and replacement; height cannot exceed 6 feet behind the building line or 4 feet in front of it.
  • Tree removal needs a permit costing $25 regardless of how many trees, with a site plan of canopy, understory and palm trees.
  • A permit stays active only with one approved inspection every six months.

If you hold a stalled permit, ask Building Services how to close it before listing.

sections.h2: Who owns which pipe at a Clermont house?
sections.html:
The city draws a firm line. Your responsibility for water begins at the point where the line meets the city-owned water meter, and for sewer it begins where your lateral connects to the city main in the street. A leak or blockage on your side is your cost, and one on the city's side is the city's.

The FAQ also says homes with water pressure of 80 psi or more need a pressure-reducing valve under building codes, and the homeowner owns and maintains it. A failing valve or lateral shows up in inspections, so check yours before you list.

sections.h2: What do Clermont's emergency services look like for insurance and buyers?
sections.html:
The Clermont Fire Department runs four stations, at 439 W Highway 50, 2200 Hartwood Marsh Road, 2155 Legends Way and 13341 Hartle Road. The city says its units average a response time under four minutes, and Lake-Sumter EMS provides the ambulance transport.

Buyers like to hear that. It is one more detail for a listing description, and you can cite the city's own page rather than guess.

sections.h2: How does Florida tax a Clermont sale?
sections.html:
For Lake County deeds the state tax is 70 cents per $100 of the price, collected by the clerk at recording, and every signer is on the hook for it. Your closing agent can show the figure ahead of any price agreement.

Each parcel is valued on January 1, exemption applications close March 1, and a November payment earns a 4 percent discount. After a sale a homestead goes back to full just value on the next January 1, so a buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Tell buyers who compare tax records.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Clermont rental house with a tenant inside?
sections.html:
Yes, and the lease usually decides what happens next. Florida ends a month-to-month tenancy with at least 30 days of notice before a monthly period closes, a year-to-year tenancy with 60 days and a week-to-week tenancy with 7. A tenant behind on rent gets 3 days of written notice, with weekends and court holidays left out of the count.

Read the lease for an end date, deposit terms and any right of entry for showings. Some cash buyers take a rented house with the lease running, so rent keeps arriving.

sections.h2: What if a Clermont owner has fallen behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Foreclosures here run through the courts. After a final judgment the clerk sets a public auction for 20 to 35 days out, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. Leftover funds go to whoever claims them before the clerk reports them as unclaimed.

A lender wanting the quicker order-to-show-cause track faces a hurdle with owner-occupied homes: a homestead exemption on the latest tax roll raises a presumption that the owner lives there. Sell before the auction and the payoff comes from the proceeds, possibly leaving equity for you. Timing questions belong with a Florida attorney or your servicer.

sections.h2: How does probate affect selling an inherited Clermont home?
sections.html:
An heir cannot sell until a court gives someone authority, normally a personal representative. A non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less may use summary administration, as may one where the owner died over two years back. The revenue department lists a representative's deed under a probated will among those that owe no deed tax.

Creditors must file within three months of the first published notice, or 30 days after a known creditor is served, whichever ends last. No Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004. Agree on dates with the probate clerk and a title company before accepting an offer.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Clermont house sell for cash?
faqs.a: Often within a few weeks, because a cash buyer skips underwriting and the appraisal. Title work and liens can still set the pace. Get the offer and the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Must a Clermont seller show a permit history?
faqs.a: A permit history is not required to list, but open permits can delay closing. Call Clermont Building Services to learn whether any permit at your address is unfinished and what inspections are needed.

faqs.q: What if my Clermont house has an old roof or unpermitted work?
faqs.a: An as-is sale is allowed, and cash buyers take houses that way. Disclose what you know, and expect a buyer to price in the repair or permit cleanup.

faqs.q: Who pays the Lake County deed tax?
faqs.a: Contracts commonly put it on the seller, though the state holds every signer liable. The charge is 70 cents per $100 of consideration; settle the point in writing.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends with the sale. The buyer must apply by March 1 for a new exemption, and the parcel returns to just value the following January 1.
